name: addERI_Proxmox_VE
description: Sets an ERI on each Proxmox VE node's resource so Proxmox_VE_Topology can attach its node vertex to it. Needs no API token.
technicalNotes:
There is no property to set: it finds a Proxmox node three ways: the API token (hasCategory("ProxmoxVE")); pve.topology.node set on the resource; or a Proxmox kernel, whose version carries -pve in system.sysinfo (from SNMP). An LXC container reports its host's kernel too, so a resource with Proxmox's guest MAC prefix bc:24:11, or pve.guest.mac_prefix, is left out of the kernel test. A node with neither SNMP nor the token, or nested Proxmox (a Proxmox VM, which carries a guest MAC), joins through pve.topology.node on its own resource.

Deliberately not gated on hasCategory("ProxmoxVE"): that category needs the API token, and the map needs this key on every node, while the token belongs on one node per cluster (docs/INSTALL.md 4.1). So the node's name comes from the API where the resource has a token, and otherwise from pve.topology.node or else the short form of system.sysname or system.hostname (Proxmox requires a node's name to be its hostname). Only a resource added by IP address with no SNMP or SSH, and so no name at all, needs pve.topology.node; without a name the module stays silent.

pve.topology.cluster is optional. Where it is set, or the resource has a token, the module also stamps the cluster-scoped key proxmoxve--<cluster>--<node>. Set it only on a group holding one cluster's nodes, never on a group spanning clusters: a wrong value can attach a node to the same-named node of another cluster. The token-holding resource publishes the exact name as auto.pve.cluster.name.

Stamps its keys in their own category "proxmoxve" so it combines with the MAC-based ERIs a monitored Linux resource already carries rather than replacing them -- keys from every category merge into predef.externalResourceID, and the resource type comes from the highest-priority entry across all categories. This module emits PhysicalServer, the type a node already has, so the priority does not change what it is drawn as.

The keys are synthesised because Proxmox exposes no hardware identifier for a node anywhere in its API: /cluster/status gives name, ip and nodeid, /nodes/{node}/status gives none, and /nodes/{node}/network has no hwaddr. VMware does not need this because vCenter hands out each ESXi host's hardware UUID. The key that needs no cluster name is proxmoxve--node--<node>--<ip>, one per address in system.ips (loopback and link-local skipped): Proxmox_VE_Topology builds the same key from the address /cluster/status reports for the node, which is among them. The name alone would collide across clusters and the address alone across overlapping networks; together they are unique in practice; an environment that reuses both collides, and topo.namespace is not supported (docs/INSTALL.md 3.3). pveTopoKey and pveTopoNodeKey in the preamble are the single definitions of the keys' shapes, and Proxmox_VE_Topology calls the same helpers -- the two must produce byte-identical keys or every node vertex silently stops matching its resource.

The node it stamps is the one the resource is, not any node in the cluster: on the API path /cluster/status marks the responding node with local=true; on the property path the resource's own hostname names it. Without that, every node would be stamped with the same key.

Limitation: not yet tested with the nodes of two clusters in one portal. The node key is the node's name plus its address, so two clusters whose nodes share both would be joined on the map.

Silent on any failure, like addCategory_Proxmox_VE: it runs against resources that may not be Proxmox, and a PropertySource that prints on a host it does not understand corrupts that resource's properties.
